text:
eli: heads up — after the KV-cache sharding change I pushed last night we're seeing a ~12% p95 tail regression on 4xA100 TP runs. repro on the integration benchmark (long-chat, seq=2048). :eyes:

maria: ugh. any flame graphs or pprof? is it steady or intermittent?

eli: steady across 10 runs. quick numbers from nightly job:
```
old: p95=48.2ms, p99=92.7ms, throughput=630 tok/s
new: p95=54.1ms, p99=103.4ms, throughput=605 tok/s
```

eli: regression spikes during prompt chunking + generation boundary when KV cache shard recombine happens. looks like extra all-gather on QKV path.

jamie: can you paste the profiler slice where comm spikes? also which kernel selection path was taken (flash vs fused-attn fallback)?

eli: attaching short trace from perf-bot summary below. flash-attn still chosen for local TP shards, but we see frequent `all_gather`/`all_to_all` calls synchronized with KV commit. snippet:
```
[trace] 0.123s compute (fused_attn)
[trace] 0.125s all_gather (KV combine)  <-- blocking
[trace] 0.140s compute (ffn)
[trace] 0.200s all_reduce (grad emulation)
```

perf-bot: nightly-bench/1766004000: 10 runs, seq=2048, model=xl-24b-tp4
summary: p95 +12.2%, p99 +11.5%, throughput -4.0%

srini: hypothesis: KV-shard recombine is not overlapped with next-token compute because batching heuristic changed shard boundaries; maybe smaller batches force sync points. did the batching window change?

eli: yes, I tightened the batch flush throttle in batching heuristics (flush when queued tokens > 512 to keep latency stable). could be causing earlier cache materialization.

leah: if cache materialization triggers an all_gather of large KV slices, that will serialize TP QKV patterns. we should try delaying KV-shard recombine until after prefix compute for next batch (if safe).

maria: let's test two experiments: 1) revert batch flush throttle to previous value and 2) enable async KV recombine (best-effort overlap). measure p95 and cpu/gpu utilization.

jamie: also try toggling env var `REDWOOD_FUSE_ALLREDUCE=1` — we had a regression tolerance letting fused all-reduce overlap with collectives. command:
```bash
REDWOOD_FUSE_ALLREDUCE=1 ./bin/infer_benchmark --tp=4 --seq=2048 --batch=8
```

eli: ran experiment 1 (revert throttle) — quick numbers:
```
revert: p95=49.0ms, p99=95.1ms, throughput=627 tok/s
```
so mostly recovered, ~1.6% higher than old baseline.

eli: experiment 2 (async recombine prototype) partial result (single run): p95=50.5ms, throughput=623 tok/s. looks promising but there are edge cases where KV indices mismatch when a flush is preempted.

srini: what about QKV all-gather pattern? if shards perform all_gather per attention head vs per-tensor it changes overhead. we should check whether current TP kernel does per-head gather causing more ops.

jamie: confirmed in kernel trace: we do per-head gather fallback on non-contiguous KV layout. The sharding change made KV layout non-contig sometimes. That explains extra calls. Fix options: 1) recontiguous KV on shard boundary, 2) change sharder to keep head-major layout, 3) modify kernel to accept strided inputs (harder).

leah: option 2 seems cheapest. but benchmark impact of the memcpy to re-layout vs extra all_gather. can we microbench re-layout cost?

eli: microbench results (512 heads x 64k elements): memcpy re-layout = 1.9ms, extra all_gather overhead across network = 6.5ms on 4xA100 with current NCCL settings. so re-layout wins.

maria: good data. eli, can you send a patch to change sharder to preserve contiguous head-major KV? add a feature flag `REDWOOD_KV_LAYOUT=head_major` so we can toggle. Also add a fast path in kernel selector to prefer flash-attn when layout is contiguous.

eli: will open PR today. I'll include regression test in nightly perf harness.

jamie: one more ask — instrument comm/compute overlap metric in the console: ratio of time spent in blocking collectives during generation window. then we can graph before/after.

perf-bot: perf-graph ticket created: PERF-4621 (ingest: comm/compute overlap metric)

srini: note for release: if we ship this sharder change, we should also test in Dedicated where inter-node topology is different (rdma vs nvlink mix). all_gather cost varies a lot.

eli: agreeing. plan: patch sharder for head-major, revert temporary throttle change, push async recombine as opt-in, add console metric. rolling tests across cloud regions and Dedicated clusters.

leah: :thumbsup: thanks for fast triage.

jamie: ping @maria once PR lands so we can run the full CI perf gate.

maria: will do. thanks all.
